links.outcome: Readability of LLM answers to hemodialysis questions versus recommended sixth-grade level
links.effect: All five models produced texts exceeding the sixth-grade reading level; ARI, GFI, FKGL, CLI, SMOG notably higher than recommended; FRES substantially below the 80-90 range.
links.quote: In terms of readability, all models produced texts exceeding the sixth-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient education content relative to recommended level
links.effect: All models exceeded sixth-grade reading level; FRES scores substantially below the 80-90 range recommended for patient materials.
links.quote: In terms of readability, all models produced texts exceeding the sixth-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Source attribution and transparency in LLM responses on hemodialysis
links.effect: All models showed limitations in information quality and transparency; persistent deficiencies in source attribution, with Perplexity performing relatively better on DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA.
links.quote: However, persistent deficiencies in source attribution, language accessibility, and response consistency limit their immediate clinical and educational utility.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the reliability and readability of 5 LLMs answering hemodialysis patient questions using standardized instruments (DISCERN, FKGL, etc.) without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
